name: 1601 Prairie Avenue — frame dwelling at the 16th Street corner, K16 clapboard

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The house claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). No source here states when 1601 was built, so no building date is claimed.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 2.000, v -5.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.615 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1601 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1601 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle inside the traced main part of s20fp-1601-b1 (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s20.json, T-2328), kept from the draft (15.5 m deep, 5.5 m along Prairie). The sheet's 'stepped outline' on the 16th Street side is the two-storey wing (form.frame_house, u 5.25-12.5, 1.5 m out), also kept from the draft's fit; the trace's narrower step at the front of that side (about 1 m, u 13-16) and its rear wall, which follows the slanted rear lot line up to 1.9 m behind the rectangle, are not built.

stories.note: '2' printed on the 1911 sheet: two full storeys, under a gable whose attic is not a storey.

construction.note: Drawn yellow, the sheet's colour for frame. Built board by board from the K16 timber kit at a frame wall's 0.15 m, never with a masonry wall's thickness or a stone texture.

frame_house.note: The whole house from the K16 kit (T-2398). READ from the sheet through the T-2328 trace s20fp-1601-b1 and the draft's fit of it: the main block's rectangle (15.5 m deep, 5.5 m along Prairie, the footprint above), two storeys, frame, and the two-storey wing standing 1.5 m out on the 16th Street side (u 5.25-12.5, the draft's r2), which is the sheet's stepped outline. Everything else is RECONSTRUCTED from the kit and recorded as L-k16-1601-frame-house-2398: clapboard on a water table over a 0.45 m foundation, corner boards, two-over-two sash in flat timber casings (two bays on the front, four a storey down the south side, two on the rear, two on the 16th Street side beyond the wing and three a storey on the wing), a four-panel door at the south end of the front (the draft rules' entrance side, away from the corner), a deep frieze under a boxed eave with scroll brackets round both blocks, a 40-degree gable with its ridge running back from the street (the draft's roof) standing on the eave as a closed pediment at the front and the rear, an attic sash in each gable, a flat deck on the lower wing, one brick stack on the ridge, a small kit entrance porch with timber steps at the door (the sheet draws no porch), and a grey-green body paint.

roof_covering.note: No roof covering has been read for 1601. A small frame house of its size was commonly shingled, and the weathered grey-brown of cedar is RECONSTRUCTED, the colour 1630's and 1638's K16 roofs use; the shingles themselves are not modelled. The wing's flat deck takes the same colour.

boundary.note: T-3230 (piece 2 of T-3216; the owner, 2026-10-27: every worked house's walk to its door and its front boundaries, and where no picture shows them a stated reconstruction consistent with the block). No picture of this front is held. The east side of the 1600 block is drawn open where it is drawn at all: 1621's and 1623's 1886 drawings and 1625's 1890 photograph show no fence or kerb on the street line (T-3221), and 1613, 1615 and 1619, unpictured, were laid open on that reading (T-3229). So this front is laid open too (`layout: open`, archetypes/k16_yard.py): nothing on the street line, the whole front between the lot lines the opening. The street line and lot lines are parcel prairie_1601's (data/street_grid/1904.json, read off the 1911 sheet) carried into the house's plan frame by the placement its sidecar holds (the transform that puts 1720's recorded street line, u 31.2, back on its parcel to the centimetre): the street line runs u 18.12 at the north lot line (s -1.70) to 18.04 at the south (s 13.20), taken as u 18.09 where the walk meets it, on the porch stair's axis (s 4.15). RECONSTRUCTED: that the front stood open in 1904 (liberty L-k16-walks-1600-block-3230).

yard.note: T-3230. A front walk in flags straight out from the porch stair's foot (read off the built steps) to the street line, the public walk's inner edge, 1.2 m wide in 0.9 m flags 0.06 m over the ground, the district's K14 walk sizes and the width 1613, 1615 and 1619 were given (T-3229). RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's line, width and surface; no picture shows them (liberty L-k16-walks-1600-block-3230). No lawn is laid: the yard's ground is the app's own (generators/archetypes/k16_yard.py).

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2-storey frame (yellow) dwelling (D), stepped outline; nothing behind it before the tracks'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2398 (piece 1 of T-1866) refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under the same id: the whole house is rebuilt from the K16 timber kit — clapboard walls built board by board on a water table, cased two-over-two sash and a panelled door, a bracketed boxed eave, a 40-degree gable standing on that eave as a closed pediment front and rear with an attic sash in each, one brick stack, a small kit entrance porch with its steps — instead of the draft builder. What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 (storeys '2', frame, use 'D', the traced main body and the two-storey wing on its 16th Street side) through the T-1840 census and the T-2328 trace. Everything else is reconstructed and recorded as L-k16-1601-frame-house-2398. No photograph, plate or description of 1601 has been read; a later reading that finds one replaces the kit's choices here.
